conviction_note: Scaled number = (2*45/100-1)*13 = -1.3: a modest down lean because the aggregator revenue bar (~$178m, two agreeing sources) looks unreachable on the company's own disclosures and the $60m 2026 pro forma EBITDA guide depends on Q4 closings that have not been announced, held near 50 because the stock has already fallen 63% off its high and 14% today with no news, and the funding stack the guide assumed is now in place. The findings sum (-3.3) is larger than the scaled number because it carries the revenue gap at full size while p_up absorbs the uncertainty about whether the covering analysts (who know closings are Q4-weighted) care about that aggregator mean.
bar: Two bars. (1) Aggregator Q3 revenue consensus $177.5m (Benzinga, per search snippet of https://www.benzinga.com/quote/TMS/earnings-forecasts, page itself 403) and $178.69m (https://www.fxempire.com/stocks/tms/earnings), EPS -$0.03 (FXEmpire, Yahoo, https://public.com/stocks/tms/earnings) to -$0.06 (Benzinga); FY2026 revenue mean $667.8m, range $620m-$732m, 4-5 analysts (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/tms/forecast/, updated 2026-10-20) - the wide range means the mean is pulled up by one high model. (2) The company bar: 2026 Pro Forma Adjusted EBITDA $60m including $40m annual adjusted EBITDA from 2026 acquisitions, reaffirmed 2026-08-14 (https://finviz.com/news/382284/teamshares-reports-2q-2026-results-and-reaffirms-2026-outlook), conditional on timely financing; $100m 2027 PF adj EBITDA forecast restated by the CEO 2026-10-19. print_vs_bar_pct is measured against bar (1): my estimate of Q3 revenue ~$150-158m vs $178m.
positioning_check: No option chain (baseline: no_options_market), so no skew and no implied move. Short interest 139.6k shares, 0.19% of float, 1.0 days to cover as of 2026-10-02 settlement (https://equibles.com/stocks/tms, via search snippet); Curved Trading lists a borrow fee of 76.9% (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/tms/, search snippet; page 403) - hard to borrow, so shorts are tiny and not crowded; no squeeze mechanism of size. Turnover ~80k shares/day (~$0.4m). Holder base: T. Rowe Price 13.0m common plus the $225m preferred, Hudson Bay 4.0m, StepStone 2.0m (PIPE/de-SPAC holders; PIPE resale S-1 effective 2026-07-31).

findings.finding: Aggregator Q3 revenue consensus is $177.5m (Benzinga) / $178.7m (FXEmpire), a 20% sequential jump from Q2's $148.7m, but the company's own disclosures leave little room for acquired revenue in Q3: only two acquisitions (~$2.6m LTM EBITDA) closed in H1, management said 2026 closings would be 'highly 4Q-weighted' with 90-120 day closes, the acquisition preferred was only funded 2026-09-23, no 8-K item 2.01 has been filed since listing (EDGAR submissions), and Q3 is seasonally about equal to Q2 with ~3-4% organic growth - so Q3 revenue near $150-158m, a ~12-15% headline miss against the aggregator mean.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: One prior public print (Q2, 2026-08-14): revenue $148.7m vs $144.8m (EarningsWhispers) / $151.1m (Benzinga), roughly in line, with a GAAP profit swing; stock +4.3%. No history of a large revenue miss; baseline history flagged untrustworthy (de-SPAC).
findings.why_not_priced: If the covering analysts had modelled Q4-weighted closings the aggregator Q3 mean would sit near $150-160m, not $178m, and FY2026 would not average $667.8m (that needs ~$398m in H2 vs $270m in H1). The headline 'misses revenue estimates' will print against that stale mean; the stock's fall prices broad scepticism but no aggregator has reset the number. Counter: the brokers on the Q2 call (Northland, Compass Point, CJS, Sidoti) heard the Q4-weighting directly, so the desks that matter may look through it.
findings.independence: Company-side evidence from different documents: Q2 release (https://finviz.com/news/382284/teamshares-reports-2q-2026-results-and-reaffirms-2026-outlook, 2 deals/$2.6m closed YTD), Q2 call transcript (https://longbridge.com/en/news/295941801, 'highly 4Q-weighted', 90-120 day closes, Q2~Q3 seasonality), EDGAR submissions list (https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0002048951.json, no item 2.01 8-K since June). Consensus side: Benzinga $177.5m (search snippet) agrees with FXEmpire.

findings.finding: The $60m 2026 Pro Forma Adjusted EBITDA guide requires ~$40m of acquired EBITDA closed by year-end; at 2026-08-14 only ~$2.6m had closed and ~$30m sat under non-binding LOI, the guide was explicitly conditional on timely financing, and the 2026-10-19 release (the company's last operating statement) spoke only of having 'signed LOIs towards our $40 million EBITDA acquisition plan' and of the $100m 2027 forecast, without restating the $60m 2026 figure or announcing any closing - so tonight's release carries real risk of a 2026 guide cut or a 'timing' push of closings into 2027.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guide reaffirmed at Q2 (2026-08-14), stock +4.3%. No cut yet in the public record; the stock fell from 9.14 (09-24) to 4.10 (10-29) without a guide change, so part of a cut is plausibly in the price.
findings.why_not_priced: Sell-side targets are still $10.90-$14 with Northland reiterating Buy/$14 on 2026-10-20 (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/tms/forecast/), and consensus FY2026 revenue ($667.8m) embeds most of the acquisition plan; if a cut were expected, targets and FY estimates would have moved. The 63% drawdown prices scepticism in general but no estimate reflects a lower 2026 number. Counter, netted into the size: the funding the guide assumed is now in place ($225m preferred, refinanced term loan) and the CEO said in September that LOIs beyond the $30m had been signed, so a reaffirmation with closings announced would rally the stock - hence the wide two-sided range.
findings.independence: Q2 call transcript (https://longbridge.com/en/news/295941801): bridge to $60m = $30m LOIs + $9m pipeline not yet at LOI + organic; 'will avoid managing to the quarter'. Q2 10-Q (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0002048951/000204895126000015/tms-20260630.htm) states guidance assumes financing closes. Sept 23 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0002048951/000204895126000020/teamshares-20260923xpressr.htm) mentions additional LOIs, unquantified - points the other way.

findings.finding: Financing answered: the $225m Series A preferred from T. Rowe Price (2026-09-23; 16% cash / PIK at a premium, non-convertible so no common dilution) funds the acquisition plan, and the $130m Sound Point term loan (funded 2026-10-16, SOFR+9.5%, matures 2030) repaid the $150m legacy facility that drove the Q2 10-Q's going-concern 'substantial doubt' (i80 facility $153.4m due 2026-12-05) - so the Q3 10-Q should lift or soften the going-concern language and cut ~$8m/yr of interest, against ~$36m/yr of preferred dividends senior to common from Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Preferred announcement 2026-09-23: +3.2% that day, +7.5% next, then -12.5% on 09-25. Refinancing 2026-10-19: +3.9%, then -11.0% on 10-21. The market has not paid for financing news beyond a day.
findings.why_not_priced: Both deals are public and the stock fell after each, so the financing itself is priced; what is not yet visible is the 10-Q's going-concern conclusion and how much of the preferred was deployed into closings by quarter-end/November. If the market had credited the removal of the maturity wall, the stock would not have made new lows (4.10) a week after the refinancing.
findings.independence: Q2 10-Q going-concern paragraph (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0002048951/000204895126000015/tms-20260630.htm); preferred terms (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0002048951/000204895126000020/teamshares-20260923xpressr.htm). Shares the Oct-19 8-K with finding 2 (different item: debt terms vs CEO quote).
